# Pin the ways ClassSystem.beforeSetInstance turns a config into an instance

## Welcome 👋

Many Neo configs accept almost anything: a class, a class name, a config object, an object with an `ntype`, or a ready instance. They all end up as one instance. That conversion is a single static method, `Neo.util.ClassSystem.beforeSetInstance()`. It is used across the engine, it is short, and it has no test. Pinning it is a great way to learn how Neo creates things.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Source: `src/util/ClassSystem.mjs`, `static beforeSetInstance(config, DefaultClass = null, defaultValues = {})`
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/util/ClassSystem.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/util/Array.spec.mjs` (the `setup()` call and imports)
- Tip: define a tiny test class in the spec (extend `Neo.core.Base`, give it a `className` and an `ntype`, register it with `Neo.setupClass`) so every row has something to create. Give it `static observable = true`, as `src/util/HashHistory.mjs` does: `core.Base` has no `on()` of its own, and the row that passes `listeners` needs one.

## What to cover

| `config` | `DefaultClass` | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | a class | a new `DefaultClass` instance built with `defaultValues` |
| `null` | a class **name** string | the name is resolved with `Neo.ns()`, then as above |
| a class | — | `Neo.create(config, defaultValues)` |
| `{ntype: '…', …}` | — | `Neo.ntype({...defaultValues, ...config})`: keys in `config` win over defaults |
| `{…}` without `ntype` | a class | `Neo.create({module: DefaultClass, ...defaultValues, ...config})` |
| an existing instance | — | the **same** instance; when `defaultValues.listeners` is given, those listeners are attached with `on()` |
| `null` | none | `null`, returned unchanged |

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/util/ClassSystem.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row, each checking the class of what comes back (and identity for the instance row).
- [ ] Test-only: if the method disagrees with a row, say so on this issue before changing `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/util/ClassSystem.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

The callers of `beforeSetInstance` and `Neo.create` itself.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.
